docs.title: CryptokiMan
docs.text:
CryptokiMan is a graphical manager and test utility for PKCS #11 (Cryptoki) libraries. It connects to a Cryptoki module supplied by a token or HSM vendor and provides a visual way to inspect slots, tokens, mechanisms, sessions, and cryptographic objects, then invoke supported PKCS #11 operations.

The information and download links in this guide are based on the supplied project index. The screenshots and feature descriptions reflect the CryptokiMan source and its user interface. Availability of an operation depends on the module, token, permissions, and license.

docs.title: Inspect a Cryptoki module and token
docs.text: Load a vendor-provided PKCS #11 library and browse its module information, slots, tokens, mechanisms, and sessions. CryptokiMan presents properties in a field-and-value table and shows contextual information in the Information and Log panels.

docs.title: Manage sessions and authentication
docs.text: Open read-only or read/write sessions, close one or all sessions for a token, log in as a user or security officer, and log out. PIN management tools provide token initialization, user-PIN initialization, and PIN changes where supported.

docs.title: Create and manage objects
docs.text:
The Objects menu supports key generation, key-pair generation, creation of data objects and key objects, object search, copy, attribute editing, and object destruction. The source includes dialogs for RSA, EC/ECDSA, EDDSA, DSA, and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) public and private key objects.

Objects are held and governed by the selected token. Whether an attribute can be changed, an object can be copied, or key material can be exported is subject to the module and token policy.

docs.title: Run cryptographic operations
docs.text:
CryptokiMan provides interfaces for random-number generation, message digests, signing, signature verification, encryption, and decryption. Operation dialogs allow a user to select a mechanism and key, enter parameters, and provide data directly or from files. Some operations support multi-part processing.

Additional tools include key wrapping and unwrapping, key derivation, operation-state handling, CSR creation, CAVP utilities, and an HSM management interface.

docs.title: Import certificates and keys
docs.text: Import workflows are available for certificates, PKCS #12/PFX bundles, and supported private-key files. Import dialogs let the user configure attributes for the resulting certificate and key objects.

docs.title: Typical workflow
docs.text:
1. Install or locate the PKCS #11 library for the token or HSM you intend to use.
  2. Start CryptokiMan and choose File > Open... to load that library. A library file can also be dragged into the main window.
  3. Browse the navigation tree and select a slot or token to inspect its information and supported mechanisms.
  4. Choose Module > Open Session. Select read/write access only when the operation requires it and the token allows it.
  5. Log in when the operation requires authentication. Select the correct role and use the PIN assigned for that role.
  6. Select an object category or use the relevant menu to run an operation. Review details, status, and errors in the Information and Log panels.
  7. Close the session when finished. Unload the Cryptoki library before loading a different module.

Only one Cryptoki library can be loaded at a time. Initialize Token can erase existing token data; use it only when you intend to initialize that token.

docs.title: Main window
docs.text:
• Navigation tree: Shows the loaded library and its slots, tokens, mechanisms, sessions, and objects.
  • Details table: Shows properties for the selected tree item or lists objects. Select an object row to inspect it; double-click or right-click for available object actions.
  • Information tab: Displays information and details for the current selection.
  • Log tab: Displays application and operation messages. The dock can be shown from File > Show log tab.
  • Menus and toolbars: Provide File, Module, Objects, Cryptography, Import, Tools, and Help commands. The View menu can show or hide toolbar buttons when available.

docs.title: Compatibility and testing
docs.text:
CryptokiMan operates through the PKCS #11 library that you load. It does not replace that library or the token's policy. Mechanisms and operations shown by the application may be unsupported or restricted by a particular token.

The supplied project index says the application was tested with a library downloaded from SoftHSM. SoftHSM provides a software token useful for development and testing; a vendor module may behave differently.

docs.title: CryptokiMan Basic Usage
docs.text: CryptokiMan is a graphical utility for working with PKCS #11 (Cryptoki) modules. It can inspect a module, its slots and tokens, and—subject to the token's capabilities and your license—manage sessions and objects or run cryptographic operations.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Install the vendor's PKCS #11 module and any required device drivers.
  2. Identify the module library file for your operating system and application architecture. For example, a 64-bit application requires a 64-bit module.
  3. Make sure the token or HSM is available. For a software test environment, SoftHSM can provide a PKCS #11 module without hardware.
  4. Have the appropriate User PIN or Security Officer (SO) PIN available if the operation requires authentication.

CryptokiMan communicates with the device through the PKCS #11 library you load. Available mechanisms, operations, and object permissions are determined by that module and token.

docs.title: Load a PKCS #11 module
docs.text:
1. Start CryptokiMan.
  2. Select File > Open... and choose the PKCS #11 library file. You can also drag the library file into the main window.
  3. Wait for the module to initialize. The navigation tree should show the library and its slots.
  4. Select a slot or token to inspect its information and supported mechanisms in the details and information areas.

Only one Cryptoki module can be loaded at a time. Close active sessions and unload the current module before loading another one.

docs.title: Open a session and log in
docs.text:
1. Select the slot or token you want to use.
  2. Choose Module > Open Session.
  3. Choose read-only access for inspection. Choose read/write access only when you need to create, change, or remove objects and the token permits it.
  4. To perform an operation that requires authentication, choose the login command and select the correct role:
  5. User for normal token operations.
  6. Security Officer (SO) for administrative tasks supported by the token.
  7. Enter the PIN assigned to that role.

Do not confuse the User PIN with the SO PIN. The token may restrict or reject operations based on the role, session type, or login state.

docs.title: Browse objects
docs.text:
After opening a session, browse the object categories in the navigation tree. Select an object or row to view its available information. Double-click or right-click an object to see the actions supported for it, such as viewing details or managing attributes.

Object visibility and editable attributes depend on the token's policy. Sensitive key values may not be readable or exportable, even when the object itself is listed.

docs.title: Run an operation
docs.text:
CryptokiMan provides dialogs for supported operations such as random data generation, digesting, signing and verification, and encryption and decryption. A typical operation is:

  1. Open the relevant command from the Cryptography menu or toolbar.
  2. Select a mechanism supported by the module.
  3. Select the required key or object, if the operation uses one.
  4. Enter the data or choose an input file, and set any required parameters.
  5. Run the operation and review the result and status messages.

For signing, decryption, or other private-key operations, the selected key must permit the requested action and the token may require an authenticated session. If an operation fails, check the selected mechanism, key attributes, session state, and the Information and Log panels.

docs.title: Close and unload
docs.text:
1. Log out when you no longer need the authenticated session.
  2. Close the session using Module > Close Session (or the corresponding session command). Close all sessions before unloading the module.
  3. Unload or close the loaded module from the Module menu before exiting or loading another library.

docs.title: Important cautions
docs.text:
• Initialize Token replaces the token's initialization state and can erase existing token data. Use it only when you intend to initialize that token.
  • PIN initialization and changes affect access to the token. Follow the device vendor's recovery and PIN policies.
  • A read/write session permits changes only when the token and the authenticated role allow them.
  • Some CryptokiMan features require a valid license. A license does not add mechanisms or permissions that the module or token does not support.

docs.title: Try with SoftHSM
docs.text: SoftHSM is a software implementation of a PKCS #11 token and can be used for development and testing. Configure SoftHSM and initialize a test token using its own documentation and utilities, then load the SoftHSM library in CryptokiMan and follow the steps above. Keep test tokens separate from production credentials and data.

docs.text: CryptokiMan checks for a valid license at startup. The comparison below describes the application controls in the current source. Actual operations also depend on the loaded PKCS #11 module, token capabilities, and token permissions.

docs.text:
Feature Valid license No valid license Load a PKCS #11 module; view slots, tokens, sessions, and object information Available Available Open and close sessions; log in and log out Available Available Initialize or finalize the PKCS #11 module Available Available Initialize a token; initialize or change its PIN Available Unavailable Generate random data and run digest operations Available Unavailable Sign, verify, encrypt, and decrypt Available Unavailable Create key objects, edit attributes, delete or copy objects Available Unavailable Import certificates, PFX files, and private keys Available Unavailable Export keys or certificates; view key material Available Unavailable Wrap, unwrap, or derive keys Available Unavailable Create a certificate signing request (CSR) Available Unavailable HSM management and CAVP tools Available Unavailable View application logs Available Unavailable

Without a valid license, CryptokiMan remains useful for loading a module, inspecting available token and object information, and managing sessions. License-restricted controls are disabled in the interface. Some operation dialogs also restrict input modes or algorithms; the exact behavior depends on the operation.

docs.title: Getting a license
docs.text: The application includes a license information dialog for requesting or importing a license. The project guide also provides a free trial license request. Restart CryptokiMan after changing the license to apply it.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• An expired, invalid, or mismatched license is treated as unlicensed.
  • A license enables application features; it does not add capabilities that the PKCS #11 module or token does not support.
  • “Available” means the application permits the action. The token may still reject it because of its mechanism support, object attributes, login state, or policy.

docs.text:

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Closes the selected session, or closes all sessions for the selected token. The dialog title changes to Close Session or Close All Sessions to show which operation was requested.

docs.text: Control Description Slot Info Read-only information for the selected slot/token.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
Button Description OK Performs the selected close operation. On success, CryptokiMan clears its recorded session handle and login state. Cancel Closes the dialog without requesting the operation.

docs.title: CryptokiMan Main Window Guide
docs.text: Navigation tree, details table, and information/log panels.

docs.title: Main areas
docs.text:
• Navigation tree: Browse the loaded Cryptoki library, slots, tokens, mechanisms, sessions, and object categories. Select an item to show related details.
  • Details and object table: Displays properties or lists of objects. Select a row for its details; double-click or right-click an object row for available actions.
  • Information and Log dock: The Information tab shows details; the Log tab displays messages. Use File > Show log tab to show the dock.
  • Menus and toolbars: Provide library, module, object, cryptographic, import, token-tool, and help commands.
  • Status bar: Shows brief application status messages.

docs.title: Basic workflow
docs.text:
1. Use File > Open... or drag a PKCS #11 library file into the window.
  2. Browse to a slot or token in the left tree and review its information.
  3. Open a session from Module > Open Session. Log in if the selected operation requires authentication.
  4. Select an object category or item to view its properties, then use the menus or object context menu to perform an operation.
  5. Check the Information and Log tabs for results and errors.

Only one Cryptoki library can be loaded at a time. Unload the current library before opening another. Available operations depend on the module, token, session, object permissions, and license.

docs.title: CryptokiMan Menu Guide
docs.text: This guide summarizes CryptokiMan's menus and the actions they provide for tokens, sessions, objects, and cryptographic operations.

docs.title: File
docs.text: Command Description New Opens another CryptokiMan window. Open... Selects and loads a Cryptoki library. Only one library can be loaded at a time. Unload Unloads the currently loaded Cryptoki library. Show log tab Shows the Information and Log dock at the bottom of the window. Recent Files Opens a previously loaded library. The menu keeps up to ten recent entries. Quit Exits CryptokiMan.

docs.title: View
docs.text: The View menu is available when the application has a valid license. Its submenus contain checkable options for showing or hiding individual buttons on the File, Module, Object, Cryptogram, Import, Tools, and Help toolbars. The Cryptogram toolbar contains the Cryptography menu commands. Changing a toolbar option does not remove the command from its main menu.

docs.title: Module
docs.text: Command Description Initialize Initializes the PKCS #11 library (C_Initialize). Finalize Finalizes the PKCS #11 library (C_Finalize). Open Session Opens a session on the selected token (C_OpenSession). Close Session Closes the selected session (C_CloseSession). Close All Sessions Closes all sessions for the selected token (C_CloseAllSessions). Login Logs in to the selected session, for example as a user or security officer (C_Login). Logout Logs out of the selected session (C_Logout).

docs.title: Objects
docs.text: Command Description Generate Key Pair Generates a public/private key pair on the token (C_GenerateKeyPair). Generate Key Generates a secret key on the token (C_GenerateKey). Create Data Creates a data object using the supplied attributes (C_CreateObject). Create RSA Public Key Creates an RSA public-key object from supplied attributes. Create RSA Private Key Creates an RSA private-key object from supplied attributes. Create ECDSA Public Key Creates an elliptic-curve public-key object, commonly used for ECDSA. Create ECDSA Private Key Creates an elliptic-curve private-key object, commonly used for ECDSA. Create EDDSA Public Key Creates an Edwards-curve digital-signature public-key object. Create EDDSA Private Key Creates an Edwards-curve digital-signature private-key object. Create DSA Public Key Creates a DSA public-key object from supplied attributes. Create DSA Private Key Creates a DSA private-key object from supplied attributes. Create PQC Public Key Creates a post-quantum cryptography public-key object supported by the library. Create PQC Private Key Creates a post-quantum cryptography private-key object supported by the library. Create Key Creates a key object from a supplied template. Destroy Object Destroys the selected token object (C_DestroyObject). Edit Object Edits attributes of the selected object. Whether an attribute can be changed depends on the token. Edit Attribute List Edits a list of attributes for the selected object. Copy Object Copies the selected object, optionally with changed attributes (C_CopyObject). Find Objects Searches the selected session for objects matching supplied attributes.

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text: Command Description Random Generates random bytes using the token (C_GenerateRandom). Digest Computes a message digest using a supported mechanism. Signature Signs data using a selected private key and signature mechanism. Verify Verifies a signature using data, a signature, and a suitable public key. Encrypt Encrypts data using a selected key and supported mechanism. Decrypt Decrypts data using a selected key and supported mechanism. HSM Manage Opens the HSM management window. Available management operations depend on the configured HSM.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: Command Description Import certificate Imports a certificate and creates a certificate object on the token. Import PFX Imports a PKCS #12/PFX file. The file may contain certificates and a private key. Import Private Key Imports a supported private-key file and creates a key object on the token.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Command Description Initialize Token Initializes the selected token (C_InitToken), including its label and security-officer PIN. Token initialization may erase existing token data. Operation State Reads or restores the state of an operation when supported by the token. Set PIN Changes a token PIN (C_SetPIN). Init PIN Initializes the user PIN (C_InitPIN), generally after security-officer authentication. Wrap Key Wraps (exports in encrypted form) a key using a wrapping key and supported mechanism. Unwrap Key Unwraps a key and creates a corresponding key object on the token. Derive Key Derives a new key from a base key using a supported mechanism. Type Name Opens the type-name utility for PKCS #11 type information. Make CSR Creates a certificate signing request (CSR) using a key and request details. CAVP Opens the Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program utility.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: Command Description Clear Log Clears the messages in the Log tab. This command is created when a valid license is present. Log Toggles logging. The command's status tip says “Halt log”; it is created when a valid license is present. Settings Opens CryptokiMan settings. License Information Displays license information. Bug or Issue Report Opens the project's bug or issue reporting page. Q and A Opens the project's Q&A or discussion page. About CryptokiMan Displays information about the application.

docs.text:
Right-click an object row to show commands for that object type. The menu is not shown for the root, slot, token, mechanism, or session tree items.

Delete Object Destroys the selected object. View Certificate Displays certificate details. Shown for certificate objects. Export Certficate Exports a certificate object. Shown for certificate objects. Verify / Encrypt Uses a public key for signature verification or encryption. Shown for public-key objects. Export PublicKey / View PublicKey Exports or displays a public key. Sign / Decrypt Uses a private key to sign or decrypt. Shown for private-key objects. Export PrivateKey / View PrivateKey Exports or displays a private key, subject to token permissions. Make CSR Creates a CSR using a private-key object. Sign / Verify / Encrypt / Decrypt Offers supported cryptographic operations for a secret-key object. Copy Object Copies the selected object. Available for certificate, public-key, private-key, secret-key, and data objects.

Commands may be disabled when the license does not enable the operation. Actual success also depends on the PKCS #11 module, token, session state, key attributes, and mechanism support.

docs.text: Command Description New Opens another CryptokiMan window. Open... Selects and loads a PKCS #11 Cryptoki library. The library provides access to the cryptographic token or HSM. Unload Unloads the currently loaded Cryptoki library. Show log tab Shows the information and log dock at the bottom of the window. Recent Files Reopens one of the recently loaded Cryptoki libraries. Quit Exits CryptokiMan.

docs.text: The View menu configures which actions appear on each toolbar. Its submenus are File ToolBar, Module ToolBar, Object ToolBar, Cryptogram ToolBar, Import ToolBar, Tools ToolBar, and Help ToolBar. Each submenu contains checkable items corresponding to the commands in the matching menu; checking an item shows that command on the toolbar, and unchecking it hides the toolbar button. The command remains available from its main menu.

docs.text:

Command Description Initialize Initializes the Cryptoki module (C_Initialize) before using its services. Finalize Finalizes the Cryptoki module (C_Finalize) and releases module state. Open Session Opens a session on the selected token (C_OpenSession). Close Session Closes the selected session (C_CloseSession). Close All Sessions Closes all sessions for the selected token (C_CloseAllSessions). Login Authenticates to the token in the selected session (C_Login), typically as a user or security officer. Logout Ends the current authenticated state for the selected session (C_Logout).

docs.title: Objects
docs.text:
Create, inspect, find, copy, edit, or destroy objects in the selected session. Availability depends on token support and object permissions.

Command Description Generate Key Pair Generates a public/private key pair on the token (C_GenerateKeyPair). Generate Key Generates a secret key on the token (C_GenerateKey). Create RSA Private Key Creates an RSA private-key object from the supplied key attributes. Create ECDSA Public Key Creates an elliptic-curve public-key object (commonly used for ECDSA). Edit Object Edits attributes of a selected object. Only attributes permitted by the token can be changed. Edit Attribute List Edits an object's attribute list in a batch-oriented editor. Copy Object Creates a copy of a selected object, optionally with changed attributes (C_CopyObject). Find Objects Searches the selected session for objects matching the specified attributes.

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text:
Run cryptographic operations through the loaded module and selected session or key.

Signature Signs data with a selected private key and signature mechanism. Verify Verifies a signature against data using a selected public key and mechanism. docs.text: Command Description Import certificate Imports a certificate and creates a certificate object on the token. docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Command Description Initialize Token Initializes a token (C_InitToken), setting its label and security-officer PIN. Initialization may erase existing token contents. Init PIN Initializes the user PIN, typically after the security officer has logged in (C_InitPIN). Wrap Key Exports a key in wrapped (encrypted) form using a wrapping key and supported mechanism. Type Name Displays or selects PKCS #11 type-name information used by the application. Make CSR Creates a certificate signing request (CSR), using a selected key and certificate-request fields.
